findings.passage: If you registered to vote by the Oct. 5 deadline and have a valid photo ID, you are approved to vote early in person.
findings.note: In her constituent newsletter she tells voters a valid photo ID is needed to vote early in person. She states the rule without comment for or against it.

findings.passage: You’ll need a valid driver’s license or state-issued ID card number and your current address.
findings.note: In her newsletter she explains what a person needs to register online: a license or state ID number plus an address.
subjects: ID number to register to vote

findings.passage: It is extremely important to check your registration before the Oct. 5 deadline even if you have voted recently.
findings.note: She urges voters to check their registration and cites a news report of a long-time voter whose registration was removed without her knowledge. Tagged as a voter-roll topic.

findings.motion: SB 10 - Culp - 3rd Reading: Bill Passed (roll call 340)
findings.note: IN House, SB 10 - Culp - 3rd Reading: Bill Passed (roll call 340), 2025-04-01: nay (tally 66–26); census gate: none.

findings.passage: “If the concern is that some of our state institutions don’t have an expiration date on these IDs, the fix is simple. Just require university IDs to have expiration dates. Don’t use this reason to make it harder to vote for thousands of college students.
findings.note: Statement issued in her name after she spoke on the House floor against Senate Bill 10, which stops college students using university IDs to vote. She suggests requiring expiration dates on university IDs instead.
subjects: college or student ID as voter ID

findings.passage: “When this bill was heard in committee, I was inspired by the number of students who showed up to testify against this bill and stand up for their right to vote.
findings.note: First lines of the same statement, on Senate Bill 10 (college IDs as voter ID).
subjects: college or student ID as voter ID
